title: Centrifuge imbalance trip with coast-down lockout
nl_spec: A centrifuge drive is protected against imbalance. Imbalance is a scaled vibration level; if it reaches VIB_MAX = 70 while healthy, latch a Trip that immediately stops the Drive. After a trip the rotor must coast to rest before it can be restarted (coast-down lockout): the Trip clears only when the operator presses Reset AND the zero-speed switch ZeroSpeed is TRUE AND the rotor has been at rest continuously for COAST_TIME = 3 seconds AND the imbalance has returned below VIB_MAX (system healthy). The Drive spins when healthy, the Lid interlock is closed (Lid = TRUE), StartCmd is TRUE, and no Trip is latched. A LockedOut output mirrors the Trip. EStop is normally-closed (TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated); when activated the Drive stops. Use one TON. Write an IEC 61131-3 Structured Text PROGRAM named centrifuge with inputs StartCmd, Imbalance, ZeroSpeed, Lid, Reset, EStop and outputs Drive, Trip, LockedOut.

interface.name: ZeroSpeed
interface.description: Zero-speed switch: TRUE = rotor at rest

interface.name: EStop
interface.description: Emergency stop, normally-closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated

safety_properties.nl: On emergency stop, the drive is off.
With the lid open, the drive is off.
While a trip is latched, the drive is off.
The drive spins only on a healthy start command with lid closed and no trip.
Positive obligation: an at-or-above-limit imbalance while healthy forces a trip.
The lockout indicator is asserted only while a trip is latched.
Positive obligation: while a trip is latched, the lockout indicator is asserted.

scenarios.description: Normal spin below the imbalance limit
Imbalance trips and stops the drive
Coast-down lockout: reset only takes after 3 s at rest, then restart
A held Reset with StartCmd still held does NOT clear the trip; releasing StartCmd then Reset clears it

notes: DRAFT - pending expert PLC review. NEW FAMILY: latched machinery-protection trip whose RESET is gated by a coast-to-rest dwell (the TON measures continuous at-rest time before a reset is permitted). Distinct from on-delay start timing and from a simple alarm latch: the timer conditions the CLEAR path, not the set path, and the positive obligation forces the trip to latch on over-limit imbalance.
